questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I wanted to go south, to a more exotic country with a different culture than what I am used to. Also, I wanted to learn Spanish.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Fairly easy. My host university provided a lot of information in advance.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I had a mentor, but I did not get to meet him, even if he was available. Also my facutly was really helpful. So if I wanted more assistance than I had, I am sure I would get it.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was easy enough. I found it 3 months in advance on a Facebook page. Would be careful with scam, but I was recommended using Idealista, which is their biggest rent and housing platform. I also found an apartment there, but choose the other apartment.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: I loved living off campus, to get to know the city as well as campus. The campus is really very central, but I lived in the city central and felt like I Got the best of both worlds. There are good public transport as well as biking opportunities, seeing as it is as flat as Copenahgen!

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Registrating for courses was a bit of a hard time. I was provided a website way before applying for courses, and this did not fully align with the courses that I could actually registrate for. A factor could be that it was not intuitive if a course would be rolling my particular semester there or not. We had to sign up for the courses before, not knowing if we would actually get them. Since there is mandatory attendance at UPV, we would also have to choose groups, which became full very quickly. It was first serve, first come. And the date for signing up for courses was not obvious, and talking to some other students, they could already sign up for groups before this sign up date. In other words, it was a bit messy. But when I got there, and got to talking to the administration, when one of the courses I really wanted to take was full, they still let me in on the course. Also, changing courses and signing off courses was very okay. They were helpful.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: International office at my faculty. Helpful people.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got all the courses that I wanted in the end.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Be up to date with all the dates, especially when signing up to groups. This is what lets you in on the course. And knowing exactly how your timetable will be, in order to sign up for groups accordingly. The more sure of the timetable from get go, the easier the process will be (I think).

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Of all six courses, 3 of them were master courses and the rest was bachelor courses.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Somewhat different. No books, fairly more practical than UCPH, which I really liked. Lectures and seminars were mandatory for most of them. Important information given at lectures/seminars was not announced. you just had to be in class or get that information by asking lecturer or peer afterwards. Also, having evening school was interesting. Had several days in which I only had classes from 18-21:30 for instance.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Data Science, MA
E-learning and Social Networks, MA
IT Project and Planning, MA
Intelligent Systems, BA
Databases and Information Systems, BA
Spanish A2, BA

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: It depends on what one is interested in, but I really recommend having the Spanish class, of your level. Also, IT Project and Planning was in Spanish, which made me learn some Spanish and connect with international people! Also, Intelligent systems, if you are into AI.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: None really.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Everything was less expensive, for sure. Public transport was free. UPV provided free gyms, rent of tennis courts, padel courts, and so on. So many good privileges!

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Everything you could think of, from my interests at least. I did not miss anything.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Signing up to a sportsteam. Its free and you get to meet new people.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Enjoy the beach, renting a car (very cheap) and go outside of Valencia to discover btoh North and South Spain. Eeating out is so cheap, tapas bars (and other cuisines) can be found literally everywhere. The city is vibrant with a lot of sightseeing opportunities as well.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Soso. It was a fun adjustment with evening school and late dinners.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Spanish people are not as open as you would think, but that might be explained with their lack of English skills. Talking to them in Spanish was hard, because they speak fast. Other than that, they are loud but that is okay.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The music, the food and siesta. Having midday off. The beaches and beautiful sites and old buildings.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Learn some spanish and engage in the Spanish culture. It so beautiful. There are a lot of organizations, both non-profit and profit, who arranges a whole load of social event throughout the entire semester. We are talking basically every day of the week, there will be something. Do not feel the pressure to do it all in the Welcome Month. There are tons of possibilities later if you are having some hard time adjusting. Also, enjoy, take on day at a time, and talk to your professors if anything is not going the way you want, study-wise. They are really really nice, and they will find a way to help you pass.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: No, not that I can think of. But they can contact me per mail, if any specific questions :)

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Moving there by myself, and having to come out of my comfortzone a lot, gave me a lot of personal growth. So cliche, but not less true.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: A natural catastrophe hitting the city, making the society close down a bit. And uni was remote-only for two months.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
